title: Best Fonts for Your CV in 2026: ATS-Safe Choices for Nigeria
excerpt: Discover the top ATS-friendly fonts that will make your Nigerian CV stand out while passing automated screening systems in 2026.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: Your CV font choice can make or break your job application in Nigeria's competitive market. With over 80% of Nigerian companies now using Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), selecting the right font isn't just about aesthetics—it's about survival in the digital screening process.

Many qualified candidates lose opportunities simply because their beautifully designed CVs use fonts that ATS systems can't properly read. This comprehensive guide reveals the best fonts for your Nigerian CV in 2026, ensuring you pass both automated systems and human reviewers.
Why Font Choice Matters for Nigerian Job Seekers

In Nigeria's evolving job market, companies like Dangote Group, MTN Nigeria, and Access Bank rely heavily on ATS to manage thousands of applications. These systems scan your CV before any human sees it, and poor font choices can result in:

items: Lost formatting that makes your CV unreadable
Missed keywords due to character recognition errors

body.text: When recruiting for positions at companies like Jumia, Flutterwave, or Nigerian banks, hiring managers report that poorly formatted CVs with illegible fonts are immediately discarded, regardless of qualifications.

items: Perfect readability across all ATS systems
Excellent spacing that prevents character confusion

Testing Your Font Choice
Before submitting your CV to companies like Dangote, MTN, or any Nigerian employer, follow these testing steps:
The Plain Text Test
1. Copy your entire CV text
2. Paste into Notepad or similar plain text editor
3. Check if all characters display correctly
4. Look for spacing issues or symbol replacements
The PDF Test
1. Save your CV as PDF
2. Open on different devices (phone, tablet, computer)
3. Zoom in and out to test readability
4. Check that fonts don't substitute automatically
The Email Test
1. Email your CV to yourself
2. Open in different email clients
3. Check mobile email appearance
4. Verify attachments open correctly
Common Font Mistakes by Nigerian Job Seekers
**Mixing Multiple Fonts**
Using different fonts for headings and body text confuses ATS systems. Stick to one font family throughout.
**Inconsistent Sizing**
Varying text sizes randomly makes your CV look unprofessional. Establish a clear hierarchy and stick to it.
**Over-Stylizing**
Excessive bold, italic, or underlined text can cause ATS parsing errors. Use formatting sparingly.
**Ignoring Spacing**
Poor line spacing or character spacing affects readability. Use standard spacing settings.

body.text: Future-Proofing Your Font Choice
As ATS technology evolves in Nigeria, these trends will shape font selection:
**AI-Enhanced Parsing**
Newer systems better handle font variations, but classics remain safest.
**Mobile-First Screening**
More Nigerian employers review CVs on mobile devices, favoring clear, readable fonts.
**International Standards**
Multinational companies operating in Nigeria follow global ATS standards.
Save multiple versions of your CV with different fonts for different industries. A Times New Roman version for banking, Arial for general corporate roles, and Calibri for tech positions.
Conclusion

Your font choice significantly impacts your job search success in Nigeria's competitive market. Arial, Calibri, and Times New Roman remain the safest choices for 2026, ensuring your qualifications reach human reviewers at companies like Dangote, MTN, and emerging startups.
Remember that while font selection is crucial, it's just one element of an effective CV. Focus on ATS-safe fonts while crafting compelling content that showcases your value to Nigerian employers.
